stories.title: Walking skeleton
stories.i_want: a Python stdlib server on 127.0.0.1 serving a Vite/React page and GET /api/health, with build, tests and CI that produce a release bundle zip
stories.so_that: every later story has its place ready and a runnable artifact exists from day one
ac: build, lint, tests are green and a bundle zip with SHA-256 is produced
the server started from the bundle
I open its URL without Node installed
the page loads and /api/health returns portal, contract and skeleton versions
stories.notes: Layout per architecture.md §2 (server/, web/). Health shape per architecture §6.

stories.title: Local security baseline
stories.i_want: loopback-only binding, a per-session token, Host/Origin checks and CSRF protection on every API route
stories.so_that: no other process or web page can read or change my repository through the portal
ac: a request without or with a wrong token
it is rejected and logged to stderr without the token
a state-changing request with a foreign Origin or Host
a write path outside the repo root, including traversal
it is refused and nothing is written
stories.notes: Refined: analysis/30-refined/REFINED_AP0102_local_security_baseline.md. Token in a user-only gitignored `.portal/` file (ADR-006 revision); `/api/health` unauthenticated; launcher token delivery is AP0110 (upstream). ADR-006. Token travels URL fragment → sessionStorage → bearer header; gate nonce is handled in EP-04.

stories.title: Upstream: --json envelope and JSON Schemas
stories.i_want: a versioned --json envelope, an error envelope, `wf.py version --json`, `next_step.py --json` in the envelope, and published JSON Schemas for every contract 1.0 tool (next, backlog, check, plan, journal, story chain, version)
stories.so_that: the portal can be built and tested against a released contract and report skeleton and contract versions
ac: it prints an envelope with `contract: 1.x` that validates against its schema
it reports skeleton version and contract version in the envelope
it prints the error envelope and exits non-zero
the contract major version is bumped
schema tests for every published schema are green and a tagged release exists
stories.notes: ADR-002. Refined: analysis/30-refined/REFINED_AP0103_upstream_json_envelope.md. Delivered in the agentic-skeleton repository (NFR-14); AI implements and tags, human + AI review. Remaining tools are AP0109.
stories.out_of_scope: Write commands, launcher, --json of backlog/check/plan/journal/story chain (AP0109), context/repo_map/gates (later stories).

stories.title: Skeleton contract client
stories.i_want: to call skeleton tools through the versioned --json envelope, validate it against the JSON Schemas and check the contract version
stories.so_that: the portal never parses Markdown and detects incompatible skeleton versions
ac: a recorded envelope of every contract tool
a skeleton whose contract major differs
a clear incompatibility message is shown and data calls are refused
a compatible minor version with unknown extra fields
stories.notes: Refined: analysis/30-refined/REFINED_AP0104_skeleton_contract_client.md. Runtime stdlib schema validator; all eight tools (order AP0109 → AP0104); recovery proposal in Settings. ADR-002. Consumes the envelope released by AP0103.

stories.title: Upstream: gates.py
stories.i_want: a gates.py tool that lists pending human gates and records approve or request-changes exactly as a human edit, attributed to the project.toml owner with date
stories.so_that: the portal never edits workflow files directly
ac: each gate is listed with artifact, gate type and age in the envelope
only the gate field changes and owner and date are recorded
I run `gates.py request-changes` with a comment
the comment is recorded and no approval is written
stories.notes: Refined: analysis/30-refined/REFINED_AP0105_upstream_gates_tool.md. `## Gates` section per artifact; ids `<type>:<path>`. ADR-002, ADR-006. Delivered in the agentic-skeleton repository (NFR-14); the portal pins the released skeleton version.

stories.title: Upstream: portal.py launcher and make portal
stories.i_want: tools/portal.py and the `make portal` target in the skeleton to download the pinned bundle, verify SHA-256, cache it in .portal/<version>/ and start it
stories.so_that: every workflow repository can start the portal
ac: the bundle is downloaded, verified, cached and started
it stops and states the requirement
stories.notes: ADR-003. Delivered in the agentic-skeleton repository (NFR-14); the portal pins the released skeleton version.

stories.title: Release bundle for make portal
stories.i_want: the portal release pipeline to publish a versioned bundle zip with SHA-256 manifest that the skeleton launcher starts
stories.so_that: I get the portal with zero setup and no Node
ac: a GitHub Release with the bundle zip and SHA-256 manifest is published
the published version pinned in a fixture repository
the portal starts for that repo without Node
a bundle built for one contract major
the portal shows an incompatibility message
the launcher starts the bundle with `--repo <root>`
it serves that repository and `--help` lists `--repo`
stories.notes: Refined: analysis/30-refined/REFINED_AP0107_bundle_launcher.md. Manifest format 1 now, `--repo`, `server_bind`, CI job with the real launcher on Linux/macOS/Windows. ADR-003. Launcher is AP0106 (skeleton v1.1.0): the release publishes `manifest.json` format 1 (`manifest`, `version`, `asset`, `size`, `sha256`, `requires_python`) next to the zip, `portal_server/` at the zip root (tools/README.md, Portal launcher). The server must not stall at bind: `HTTPServer.server_bind` calls `getfqdn()` (reverse DNS, seconds on macOS); override it as the launcher tests do.

stories.notes: ADR-002. Split from AP0103 (workshop 2026-10-19). Delivered in the agentic-skeleton repository (NFR-14).

stories.title: Upstream: launcher delivers the session token
stories.i_want: tools/portal.py to generate the session token, store it in a user-only file in .portal/, pass it to the server as PORTAL_TOKEN and open the URL with #token=…
stories.so_that: the browser authenticates on first open and a reused running portal opens the same session
ac: the URL carries the token in the fragment and the server accepts it
only the current user can read it (0600; icacls on Windows, warning if it fails)
a portal already running for the repo
the running one opens with the same token read from the file
stories.notes: ADR-006 revision 2026-10-20. Delivered in the agentic-skeleton repository (NFR-14); AI implements and tags, human + AI review. Created by the workshop of 2026-10-20 (owner: fix it now); consumed by AP0102 end to end and by the AP0107 CI job. Release plan placement is open (PLAN.md).
